title: Towards Foundation Models for Knowledge Graph Reasoning

relations.condition: zero-shot link prediction on unseen KGs with arbitrary relation vocabularies; single pre-trained model vs. graph-specific trained baselines
relations.note: often on par or better than strong baselines without any task-specific training
generalizes inductive KG reasoning to any unseen graph with any relation vocabulary via relational representations conditioned on interactions
demonstrates zero-shot transfer across 57 KGs; fine-tuning further boosts performance, validating the foundation model paradigm for KGs

title: InteractE: Improving Convolution-based Knowledge Graph Embeddings by Increasing Feature Interactions

relations.condition: link prediction MRR on FB15k-237: +9%, WN18RR: +7.5%, YAGO3-10: +23%
relations.note: increased feature interactions via permutation and circular convolution drive gains
adds feature permutation, novel reshaping, and circular convolution to ConvE's 2D convolutional approach
validates that increasing feature interaction is beneficial for link prediction across three benchmarks

title: KEPLER: A Unified Model for Knowledge Embedding and Pre-trained Language Representation

relations.condition: standalone PLMs cannot effectively capture relational facts from KGs; KE-only models cannot leverage textual information
relations.note: factual knowledge capture is a known weakness of PLMs

relations.condition: inductive KG link prediction; KEPLER encodes unseen entities via text descriptions, outperforming transductive KE baselines
relations.note: text-enhanced KE via PLM encoder enables inductive generalization
jointly optimizes KE objective and language modeling objective on top of a PLM encoder
achieves SOTA on NLP tasks while also excelling at KG link prediction

title: Learning Hierarchy-Aware Knowledge Graph Embeddings for Link Prediction

relations.condition: symmetry/antisymmetry/inversion/composition-focused models cannot model entity hierarchical levels present in real-world KGs
relations.note: existing approaches focus on relation patterns and miss semantic hierarchies

relations.condition: link prediction on standard benchmarks (FB15k-237, WN18RR); significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods
relations.note: polar coordinate system maps entities to hierarchical levels via radial coordinate
HAKE models both relation patterns and semantic hierarchies, going beyond symmetry/antisymmetry/inversion/composition
polar coordinate system naturally reflects hierarchy via concentric circles

title: Modeling Relational Data with Graph Convolutional Networks

relations.note: adapts GCNs specifically to handle highly multi-relational data characteristic of knowledge bases

relations.condition: link prediction on FB15k-237: +29.8% when using R-GCN encoder combined with DistMult decoder vs. decoder-only DistMult
relations.note: GCN encoder accumulates evidence over multiple inference steps, substantially improving factorization baselines

relations.condition: standard GCNs designed for simple undirected graphs; cannot handle edge labels and directions in relational graphs
relations.note: R-GCN was developed specifically to address this limitation

title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks

relations.condition: semi-supervised node classification on citation networks; GCN outperforms related methods by a significant margin
relations.note: encodes both local graph structure and node features via localized first-order spectral convolution
uses localized first-order approximation of spectral convolutions, making it scalable (linear in graph edges)
GCN's neighborhood aggregation is equivalent to a form of message passing on the graph

title: A Review of Relational Machine Learning for Knowledge Graphs

relations.note: latent feature models like tensor factorization are a foundational class of KG embedding methods

relations.condition: scalable to large KGs; both tensor factorization and neural multiway models scale
relations.note: review establishes two scalable paradigms: latent features and observable patterns

relations.condition: complementary to latent feature models; combining both improves modeling power at decreased computational cost
relations.note: hybrid latent+observable models outperform either alone
example of combining statistical KG models with text-based information extraction for large-scale automated KG construction

title: KG-BERT: BERT for Knowledge Graph Completion

relations.note: encodes entity and relation descriptions of a triple as text input to BERT, using language model as scoring function

relations.condition: triple classification and relation prediction tasks on multiple benchmark KGs; achieves state-of-the-art
relations.note: text descriptions of entities and relations provide rich semantic signal beyond structure-only embeddings
textual descriptions encode semantic knowledge that improves over structure-only KG embeddings

relations.condition: existing multi-relational GCN approaches suffer from over-parameterization and are restricted to learning node-only representations
relations.note: edge labels and directions are not jointly embedded with nodes

relations.condition: link prediction, node classification, and graph classification on multi-relational graphs; demonstrably superior results
relations.note: joint embedding of nodes and relations, leveraging KGE composition operations
leverages entity-relation composition operations from KGE (TransE, DistMult, etc.) within a GCN framework
generalizes several existing multi-relational GCN methods and scales with number of relations

title: PairRE: Knowledge Graph Embeddings via Paired Relation Vectors

relations.condition: existing distance-based methods cannot simultaneously handle complex relations (N-to-1, 1-to-N, N-to-N) AND encode symmetry/antisymmetry/inverse/composition patterns
relations.note: tradeoff between complex relation handling and relation pattern encoding forces unsatisfactory results

relations.condition: link prediction on Open Graph Benchmark KG datasets; sets new state-of-the-art on two OGB benchmarks
relations.note: paired relation vectors enable adaptive margin adjustment for complex relations while encoding key relation patterns
adds paired vectors per relation enabling subrelation encoding and complex relation handling beyond TransE-style single vector
demonstrates encoding of symmetry/antisymmetry, inverse, composition, and subrelation patterns within one model
